In brief

Telemachus employs metaphor evocatively when it describes Mulligan’s friend moving “frogwise his green legs in the deep jelly of the water.” But when Mulligan too has dived into the seawater, and Stephen glimpses him at the end of the episode as “A sleek brown head, a seal’s, far out on the water, round,” something more than metaphor is accomplishing the metamorphosis of man into beast. The sentence describes Stephen's perceptual uncertainty about what he is seeing.

At more length

Seals abound in the waters of Dublin Bay, and food tossed to them from piers has habituated many of them to human contact. Seeing a head bobbing in the waves, Stephen might well do a double take before deciding if it was human or not. Slicked-back human heads are "sleek," "brown," "round," just like a seal's.

John Hunt 2011
